notice: 500 original practice questions. Independent educational material, not official RSA questions. Laws and guidance can change; verify against current RSA, Irish legislation and applicable EU/ADR rules. Some specialist scenarios require review by a qualified instructor.

topics.name: Road signs & signals
topics.note: Warning signs alert to hazards; regulatory signs impose requirements or prohibitions; information signs guide. A Garda direction takes precedence over traffic lights and signs.

topics.name: Rules of the road
topics.note: Drive on the left. Obey signs, signals, speed limits and road markings. Adapt speed to conditions and protect vulnerable road users.

topics.name: Vehicle checks & defects
topics.note: Check tyres, lights, mirrors, brakes, steering, fluids, wipers, coupling security and warning devices. Never use an unsafe vehicle.

topics.name: Loads & load security
topics.note: Never exceed plated weights or axle limits. Distribute weight evenly and secure it against movement.

topics.name: Trailers & couplings
topics.note: Confirm the coupling is compatible, fully engaged and locked. Check safety devices, trailer brakes, tyres and lights.

topics.name: Tachographs & drivers’ hours
topics.note: Standard EU rules include 9 hours daily driving (10 hours twice weekly), 56 hours weekly and 90 hours over two weeks. After 4.5 hours driving, take 45 minutes break, splittable 15 then 30. Exemptions apply.

topics.name: Braking & stopping distances
topics.note: Stopping distance is thinking distance plus braking distance. Speed, mass, poor grip, gradient and brake condition affect it. Use generous following gaps.

topics.name: Risk & eco-driving
topics.note: Scan ahead, anticipate hazards, maintain space and avoid harsh acceleration and braking. Fatigue, distraction, weather and poor visibility increase risk.

topics.name: Dangerous goods
topics.note: ADR may regulate classification, packaging, marking, documents, equipment, training and exemptions. Check current ADR and Irish rules.

topics.name: Bus passenger safety
topics.note: Stop safely for boarding and alighting. Move only when doors are closed and passengers are safely accommodated. Use accessibility equipment correctly.

topics.name: Vehicle dimensions & weight
topics.note: Know loaded height, width, length and permitted weights. Plan routes around restrictions and overhead clearances.

topics.name: Breakdowns & emergencies
topics.note: Protect people first, warn traffic when safe and follow emergency procedures. Call 112/999 for emergency assistance.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A triangular warning sign is approaching?
options: reduce speed and prepare for the hazard
ignore it unless traffic is present
accelerate to pass it quickly
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead.

questions.question: What is the safest response when approaching a zebra crossing with pedestrians waiting?
options: slow down and be prepared to stop
sound the horn to make them hurry
overtake a vehicle that has stopped
questions.explanation: Drivers must approach crossings carefully and give way as required.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a tyre has a deep cut or exposed cords?
options: do not use the vehicle until the defect is rectified
inflate it and continue
cover the damage with tape
questions.explanation: Tyre structural damage can cause sudden failure.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load could slide forward during emergency braking?
options: use suitable restraints against forward movement
rely on friction alone in every case
place loose material on top
questions.explanation: Loads must be restrained against forces in normal driving and emergency manoeuvres.

questions.question: What is the safest response when coupling a trailer to a tractor unit?
options: check compatibility, engagement and locking indicators
assume it has coupled because the trailer is raised
pull away without checking
questions.explanation: A visual and physical coupling check helps prevent trailer separation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you reach 4 hours 30 minutes of cumulative driving?
options: take a 45-minute break unless a valid split-break arrangement applies
take a 15-minute break only
continue until 5 hours
questions.explanation: The standard EU break is 45 minutes after 4.5 hours driving.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle's speed is doubled?
options: recognise that braking distance can increase by roughly four times under otherwise similar conditions
expect braking distance to double exactly
expect no change
questions.explanation: Braking distance rises approximately with the square of speed in idealised conditions.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you feel sleepy while driving?
options: stop at a safe place and take appropriate rest
open a window and continue indefinitely
turn up the radio
questions.explanation: Fatigue impairs attention and reaction; do not drive when unfit.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a package may contain dangerous goods but its contents are unknown?
options: do not accept or handle it until correctly identified
open it to smell the contents
assume it is ordinary freight
questions.explanation: Dangerous goods must be identified before applying handling and transport rules.

questions.question: What is the safest response when passengers are still boarding?
options: remain stopped until boarding is complete and it is safe to move
move slowly while doors are open
sound the horn to hurry passengers
questions.explanation: The bus should move only when boarding is complete and doors are closed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when your loaded vehicle is taller than a bridge's signed clearance?
options: do not proceed; choose a suitable alternative route
drive slowly under the bridge
follow a lower vehicle through
questions.explanation: A vehicle must not exceed a height restriction.

questions.question: What is the safest response when your vehicle breaks down on a high-speed road?
options: protect yourself and others and get to a safe place if possible
attempt repairs in a live lane
stand behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes first; follow the road's breakdown procedure.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A red-bordered circular sign is displayed?
options: treat it as an information sign
ignore it if the road is clear
obey the restriction shown by its symbol
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circular signs generally indicate prohibitions or restrictions.

questions.question: What is the safest response when turning left across a cycle lane?
options: turn without checking because you signal
accelerate across the lane
check mirrors and blind spots and give way to cyclists
questions.explanation: Cyclists may be alongside; check carefully before turning.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a brake warning lamp remains illuminated?
options: ignore it if the parking brake is released
disconnect the warning buzzer
investigate and resolve the fault before driving
questions.explanation: A brake warning may indicate a serious safety defect.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load is much heavier on one side?
options: leave it if gross weight is below the limit
inflate tyres on the heavier side
redistribute it to avoid uneven axle loading and instability
questions.explanation: Uneven loading can overload an axle and affect handling.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the fifth-wheel jaws may not be locked?
options: test it at road speed
rely on the air lines to hold it
do not move until the coupling is correctly engaged and locked
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel must securely lock around the kingpin.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you split the standard 45-minute driving break?
options: take 30 minutes followed by 15 minutes
take three 15-minute periods
take at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes
questions.explanation: The permitted split is at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a heavy vehicle is fully laden?
options: assume load has no effect
follow closer because the vehicle is heavier
allow for the vehicle's mass and condition when judging stopping distance
questions.explanation: Vehicle mass and braking performance affect stopping behaviour.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you approach a blind bend?
options: overtake if the road seems quiet
sound the horn and use the centre line
reduce speed and keep well within your lane
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop within the road you can see to be clear.

questions.question: What is the safest response when dangerous goods are offered for carriage?
options: rely only on the sender's verbal assurance
remove labels to avoid alarm
check classification, packaging, marking and documentation requirements
questions.explanation: ADR controls include classification, packaging, marks, labels and documents.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger using a wheelchair boards?
options: leave the wheelchair unsecured
place luggage in the wheelchair space
use the designated space and approved restraint system as instructed
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle's accessibility equipment and securement procedure.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a route has a weight-restricted bridge?
options: cross if the bridge looks strong
drive over the centre line
check the vehicle's relevant weight against the restriction and use another route if necessary
questions.explanation: Weight restrictions must be obeyed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are involved in a collision?
options: leave without checking for injuries
move injured people unnecessarily
stop, make the scene safe where possible and provide required details and assistance
questions.explanation: Drivers involved in collisions have duties to stop and provide assistance and details.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A Garda is directing traffic against a traffic signal?
options: copy the vehicle ahead
follow the Garda's direction when safe
obey the signal regardless
questions.explanation: A Garda's direction takes precedence over traffic signals.

questions.question: What is the safest response when approaching a roundabout?
options: change lanes abruptly on the roundabout
choose the correct lane and follow signs and road markings
always use the left lane for every exit
questions.explanation: Lane choice and signals depend on the exit and road markings.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a headlamp is not working before a night journey?
options: drive faster to reduce exposure
have it repaired before setting out
use hazard lights instead
questions.explanation: Required lighting must be in working order.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle's gross weight would exceed its plated limit?
options: inflate tyres to increase capacity
remove or redistribute load until within permitted limits
drive only on quiet roads
questions.explanation: The plated maximum weight must not be exceeded.

questions.question: What is the safest response when connecting trailer air lines?
options: leave a line disconnected for short trips
connect the correct lines securely and check for leaks
swap line colours if they fit
questions.explanation: Correct air connections are essential for trailer braking.

questions.question: What is the safest response when planning daily driving under the standard EU rule?
options: drive 12 hours if the vehicle is a bus
normally keep driving to 9 hours, with 10 hours allowed twice weekly
drive 10 hours every day
questions.explanation: The normal daily driving limit is 9 hours, extendable to 10 hours twice a week.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the road surface is wet?
options: brake later to keep traffic flowing
increase following distance and reduce speed
use the same gap as on dry roads
questions.explanation: Wet surfaces reduce grip and can increase stopping distances.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you see children near the roadside?
options: maintain speed to avoid confusing them
anticipate sudden movement and reduce speed
assume they will remain on the footpath
questions.explanation: Children may move unpredictably; prepare to stop.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a driver is assigned an ADR-regulated load?
options: borrow another driver's certificate
ensure required training and certificate are valid for the task
assume an ordinary driving licence is sufficient
questions.explanation: Some dangerous-goods carriage requires specialised driver training and certification.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger is standing near the doors?
options: close the doors against them
ensure passengers are safely accommodated before moving
accelerate gently to help them balance
questions.explanation: Passengers must be safely positioned before the bus moves.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are planning a route for an articulated vehicle?
options: assume every road accommodates heavy vehicles
check restrictions for height, width, length and weight
use a car navigation route without checking
questions.explanation: Route planning must account for the vehicle's actual dimensions and mass.

questions.question: What is the safest response when someone is seriously injured?
options: give food or drink
call 112 or 999 and follow the operator's instructions
move them immediately in every case
questions.explanation: Emergency services can provide guidance; avoid unnecessary movement of injured people.

questions.question: What is the safest response when An amber traffic light appears as you approach?
options: stop if you can do so safely
accelerate in every situation
reverse immediately
questions.explanation: Amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping could cause an accident.

questions.question: What is the safest response when reversing a large vehicle?
options: avoid reversing where possible and use a competent guide if needed
rely only on mirrors
reverse quickly to minimise delay
questions.explanation: Large vehicle blind spots make reversing especially hazardous.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a mirror is loose and cannot hold its position?
options: repair it before driving
adjust it once and ignore movement
drive using only the interior mirror
questions.explanation: Drivers need secure, correctly adjusted mirrors for observation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load projects beyond the vehicle?
options: ensure it is within legal requirements and properly marked where required
assume any projection is allowed at night
leave it unmarked if the journey is short
questions.explanation: Projections must comply with dimensional and marking rules.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a trailer breakaway device is fitted?
options: connect and route it as specified by the manufacturer
tie it to a movable part of the coupling
leave it disconnected
questions.explanation: A breakaway device is intended to activate braking if separation occurs.

questions.question: What is the safest response when planning a driver's weekly driving?
options: do not exceed 56 hours in a week
do not exceed 60 hours in a week
use 56 hours as a daily limit
questions.explanation: The standard weekly driving limit is 56 hours.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you descend a long steep gradient?
options: select a suitable low gear before the descent and use appropriate auxiliary braking
coast in neutral
keep the clutch depressed
questions.explanation: Engine braking and appropriate gear selection help prevent brake overheating.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are driving in strong crosswinds?
options: reduce speed and be alert to exposed sections and high-sided vehicle movement
increase speed to stabilise the vehicle
steer abruptly against every gust
questions.explanation: High-sided vehicles are vulnerable to crosswinds.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a dangerous-goods package is damaged and leaking?
options: keep clear, avoid contact and follow emergency instructions
handle it with bare hands
wash it into a drain
questions.explanation: A leak may expose people and the environment; follow emergency procedures.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger asks to alight between designated stops?
options: stop only where permitted and safe under the service rules
stop immediately in a live lane
open the doors while moving
questions.explanation: Passenger safety and stopping restrictions must be observed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load makes the vehicle wider than usual?
options: ensure the movement complies with legal limits and any required permissions
drive close to the kerb
assume warning lights make any width lawful
questions.explanation: Abnormal dimensions may require special conditions or authorisation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle fire starts?
options: stop safely, evacuate people and call emergency services
open the engine compartment fully immediately
continue to the next exit
questions.explanation: Evacuate and raise the alarm; do not put yourself at risk.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A green traffic light is showing but the junction is blocked?
options: enter and block the junction
sound the horn until traffic moves
wait until your exit is clear
questions.explanation: A green signal does not permit you to obstruct a junction.

questions.question: What is the safest response when driving on a narrow rural road?
options: assume oncoming traffic will reverse
drive partly on the footpath
reduce speed and be prepared to stop at a safe passing place
questions.explanation: Narrow roads require speed adjustment and consideration for other users.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the steering feels unusually loose?
options: continue if the road is straight
increase speed to test it
stop safely and arrange inspection
questions.explanation: Steering defects can cause loss of control.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a curtain-sided trailer carries a dense load?
options: assume the curtain alone secures all cargo
place all weight against the rear doors
use suitable load restraint; curtains are not automatically load restraints
questions.explanation: Curtains may not be designed to restrain a load unless specifically rated.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a trailer's electrical plug is connected?
options: assume the plug guarantees all lamps work
check only the brake lights
check trailer lights and indicators operate correctly
questions.explanation: A walk-around check should confirm all required trailer lights operate.

questions.question: What is the safest response when checking driving over two consecutive weeks?
options: keep total driving within 112 hours
count only the first week
keep total driving within 90 hours
questions.explanation: The two-week cumulative driving limit is 90 hours.

questions.question: What is the safest response when brakes smell hot after a long descent?
options: pour cold water on hot brakes
continue downhill using the same technique
stop in a safe place and allow them to cool; seek help if performance is affected
questions.explanation: Overheated brakes can fade and may be damaged; follow safe procedures.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you want to reduce fuel consumption?
options: accelerate hard then brake late
leave the engine idling unnecessarily
anticipate traffic and use smooth acceleration and braking
questions.explanation: Smooth, anticipatory driving reduces fuel use and wear.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are unsure whether an ADR exemption applies?
options: assume small loads are always exempt
ignore placarding rules
verify the exact provision and conditions before relying on it
questions.explanation: Exemptions have defined conditions and cannot be assumed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you approach a bus stop with pedestrians nearby?
options: swerve sharply into the stop
stop wherever passengers wave
approach cautiously and position the bus safely
questions.explanation: Safe positioning protects passengers and other road users.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are close to the permitted gross vehicle weight?
options: estimate from suspension height
ignore axle limits if gross weight is legal
check actual weight and axle distribution
questions.explanation: Both gross and axle limits must be respected.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a tyre bursts while driving?
options: brake sharply
swerve onto the hard shoulder immediately
hold the steering firmly, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually
questions.explanation: Smooth control helps maintain stability after a tyre failure.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A temporary roadworks sign conflicts with your usual route?
options: drive around the barrier
obey the temporary traffic control
follow your usual route regardless
questions.explanation: Temporary traffic controls must be obeyed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when approaching an emergency vehicle using warning lights?
options: follow closely behind it
make way safely without creating another hazard
brake sharply wherever you are
questions.explanation: Facilitate emergency vehicles when safe and legal.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the windscreen wipers smear badly in rain?
options: drive faster to clear the screen
replace or repair them before driving in conditions requiring them
use a cloth while moving
questions.explanation: Clear visibility is essential; defective wipers must be rectified.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a pallet is damaged and unstable?
options: place it above stable pallets
reject or safely repackage it before transport
strap it loosely and hope
questions.explanation: Unstable packaging can collapse or shift during transit.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the trailer parking brake is still applied?
options: ignore it because the tractor can pull it
release it only after coupling and checks are complete and it is safe
drag the trailer to free the brakes
questions.explanation: Moving with a parking brake applied can damage equipment and compromise safety.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a driver takes a regular daily rest under the standard rule?
options: replace daily rest with a meal break
allow at least 11 consecutive hours, subject to permitted reductions
take 8 hours every day
questions.explanation: The standard regular daily rest is at least 11 consecutive hours; specific reductions and conditions apply.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you approach a queue on a motorway?
options: use hazard lights instead of braking
look well ahead and slow progressively
wait until close then brake sharply
questions.explanation: Early observation and smooth deceleration reduce collision risk.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a warning of driver fatigue appears in your cab?
options: assume it is only a suggestion
take it seriously and stop safely if tired
disable it and continue
questions.explanation: Fatigue warnings should prompt an honest assessment of fitness to drive.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you carry dangerous goods in a vehicle requiring placards?
options: use handwritten substitutes
display the prescribed placards and marks correctly
cover them during the journey
questions.explanation: ADR specifies when and how placards and marks must be displayed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a child is crossing in front of the bus?
options: sound the horn and proceed
remain stopped until the child is clear and it is safe
move as soon as the child disappears from the mirror
questions.explanation: Children may be hidden in blind spots; ensure the area is clear.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle's rear overhang is substantial?
options: assume the rear follows the front wheels
allow for swing when turning and manoeuvring
turn tightly beside pedestrians
questions.explanation: Rear overhang can swing out and strike objects or people.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle begins to skid?
options: accelerate hard
avoid harsh inputs and steer smoothly in the direction needed to regain control
slam on the brakes
questions.explanation: Gentle, controlled responses help recover grip.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A STOP sign is at a junction?
options: stop at the line and proceed only when safe
slow down without stopping
stop only if another vehicle appears
questions.explanation: A STOP sign requires a complete stop at the stop line.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle ahead stops at a pedestrian crossing?
options: stop and do not overtake it
pass it if your lane looks clear
sound the horn and continue
questions.explanation: A stopped vehicle may be yielding to pedestrians hidden from your view.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the engine oil warning indicates dangerously low pressure?
options: stop safely as soon as possible and switch off the engine
continue to the next scheduled service
rev the engine to clear the warning
questions.explanation: Low oil pressure can cause severe engine damage.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load contains loose granular material?
options: contain it to prevent spillage and secure any cover
leave the body uncovered
overfill above safe body capacity
questions.explanation: Loads must not spill or create danger to road users.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a trailer tyre is underinflated?
options: correct the pressure to the specified value before the journey
increase speed to warm it
ignore it if the tread looks good
questions.explanation: Incorrect tyre pressure can cause overheating, instability and failure.

questions.question: What is the safest response when planning a regular weekly rest?
options: allow at least 45 consecutive hours, subject to permitted reductions and compensation rules
take 24 hours every week without compensation
replace it with 11 hours
questions.explanation: The regular weekly rest is 45 hours; reduced weekly rest has specific conditions and compensation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle is following very closely behind?
options: maintain a safe gap ahead and avoid sudden braking where possible
brake-check the following driver
speed up beyond the limit
questions.explanation: A larger gap ahead gives more room to respond smoothly.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are approaching a vulnerable road user?
options: slow down and give them space
expect them to move out of your way
pass as close as possible
questions.explanation: Vulnerable road users need additional care and clearance.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you receive written emergency instructions for dangerous goods?
options: keep them accessible in the cab and know how to use them
leave them with the dispatcher
store them beneath the load
questions.explanation: Written instructions inform the crew how to respond to an incident.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger falls while the bus is moving?
options: stop safely and assess the passenger before continuing
continue to the terminus
ask another passenger to deal with it while moving
questions.explanation: A fall requires the driver to stop safely and assess the situation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you approach a low tree canopy?
options: check clearance and avoid contact with overhead obstacles
accelerate to pass beneath it
assume the cab height is the vehicle height
questions.explanation: The highest point of the loaded vehicle determines clearance needs.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you see a warning of a tunnel incident?
options: follow signs and instructions and do not enter a closed tunnel
continue because your destination is close
stop in a traffic lane to take a photo
questions.explanation: Tunnel control instructions are designed to protect road users.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A YIELD sign is at a junction?
options: assume you have priority
stop in the middle of the junction
give way to traffic on the major road
questions.explanation: Yield means give way and proceed only when safe.

questions.question: What is the safest response when joining a motorway?
options: force other traffic to brake
stop at the end of the slip road if avoidable
match traffic speed where possible and join only when a safe gap exists
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to join safely without forcing traffic to react.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a wheel nut appears loose?
options: tighten it only by hand and proceed
ignore it if no vibration is felt
do not continue until the wheel fixing is checked and secured
questions.explanation: Loose wheel fixings can lead to wheel detachment.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load is stacked high?
options: assume height has no effect on handling
place heavy items at the top
consider centre of gravity and stability and secure it appropriately
questions.explanation: A high centre of gravity increases rollover risk.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a trailer is uncoupled on soft or uneven ground?
options: rely on the landing legs on any surface
leave it without its parking brake
choose firm, level ground where possible and secure it properly
questions.explanation: Stable ground and proper support reduce the risk of trailer movement or collapse.

questions.question: What is the safest response when using a digital tachograph?
options: use another driver's card if yours is lost
leave the card in the office
use your own driver card and ensure activities are recorded correctly
questions.explanation: Driver cards identify the driver and record relevant activity.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the road is icy?
options: make abrupt steering inputs
use cruise control
use very gentle controls and greatly increase stopping distance
questions.explanation: Ice greatly reduces tyre grip and increases stopping distances.

questions.question: What is the safest response when visibility is poor due to fog?
options: use high beam in dense fog
follow the tail lamps ahead closely
reduce speed and use appropriate lights
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that permits stopping within the visible clear distance.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a dangerous-goods vehicle is involved in an incident?
options: attempt to clean up an unknown spill yourself
move leaking packages without protection
protect people, call emergency services as appropriate and follow instructions
questions.explanation: Prioritise life safety and avoid exposure to hazardous substances.

questions.question: What is the safest response when an emergency exit is obstructed by luggage?
options: leave it if the journey is short
cover it with a notice
have the obstruction removed
questions.explanation: Emergency exits and access routes must remain unobstructed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you need to cross a narrow road with a wide vehicle?
options: force oncoming traffic onto the verge
mount the footpath
assess the full width and wait until it can be done safely
questions.explanation: Large vehicle width requires careful assessment and consideration of other users.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load falls onto the carriageway?
options: leave it in the road
attempt retrieval while standing in live traffic
stop safely, warn others if possible and contact the relevant authorities
questions.explanation: A fallen load creates an immediate hazard; protect people and alert authorities.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A level crossing warning is displayed?
options: stop on the tracks to check
approach cautiously and obey crossing signals
overtake near the crossing
questions.explanation: Level crossings require careful approach and strict obedience to signals.

questions.question: What is the safest response when leaving a motorway?
options: cross solid lines at the last moment
signal in good time and use the exit lane
slow dramatically in the live lane
questions.explanation: Plan exits early and use the designated lane.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle's air pressure warning activates?
options: ignore it if the vehicle still moves
stop safely and follow the manufacturer's procedure
pump the brake pedal repeatedly while moving
questions.explanation: Air pressure faults can compromise heavy-vehicle braking.

questions.question: What is the safest response when straps show cuts or damaged stitching?
options: use extra damaged straps instead
replace defective restraints before use
tie knots in damaged webbing
questions.explanation: Damaged restraints may fail under load.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the landing legs are not fully raised?
options: use them as extra rear supports
raise and secure them before moving
drive slowly with them down
questions.explanation: Landing legs left down can strike the road and cause loss of control.

questions.question: What is the safest response when your driver card is lost or stolen?
options: borrow a colleague's card
follow the legal procedure for printouts, identification and replacement
continue indefinitely without records
questions.explanation: Specific temporary procedures apply; never use another driver's card.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are driving a vehicle with an anti-lock braking system?
options: assume ABS shortens every stopping distance
apply firm continuous brake pressure in an emergency and steer as appropriate
pump the brake pedal rapidly
questions.explanation: ABS helps maintain steering control but does not remove the need for safe speed and distance.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are distracted by a navigation device?
options: hold it while steering
set it before moving and do not interact while driving
read complex instructions while moving
questions.explanation: Distraction reduces awareness and control.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are loading incompatible dangerous goods?
options: rely on the driver to separate them later
check segregation requirements and do not load incompatible items together
place them adjacent if both are packaged
questions.explanation: ADR segregation rules prevent dangerous interactions between substances.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger becomes abusive?
options: make a sudden stop to intimidate them
remain calm, avoid escalation and follow company safety procedures
argue while driving
questions.explanation: Professional de-escalation protects passengers and the driver.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are driving a long vehicle around a corner?
options: cut across pedestrian space
allow for off-tracking and rear swing
follow the exact path of a car
questions.explanation: Long vehicles need extra turning space and observation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are first at the scene of a collision?
options: assume others have called
stop only where safe, protect the scene and summon help if needed
park in a way that blocks emergency access
questions.explanation: Early safe assistance can prevent further collisions and get help moving.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A flashing amber signal is operating at a pedestrian crossing?
options: proceed only if the crossing is clear of pedestrians
assume pedestrians must wait
accelerate without checking
questions.explanation: Flashing amber requires giving way to pedestrians on the crossing.

questions.question: What is the safest response when driving in heavy rain?
options: increase following distance and reduce speed
use cruise control regardless of grip
drive close to the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distances.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load obscures a required lamp or number plate?
options: reposition or secure the load so required items are visible
leave it because the journey is short
use a torch instead of the lamp
questions.explanation: Loads must not obscure required lights, reflectors or registration plates.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are unsure of the load's weight?
options: obtain reliable weight information before loading or setting out
estimate by appearance only
assume the dispatch note is always correct
questions.explanation: Weight must be known sufficiently to ensure limits are not exceeded.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the trailer ABS warning behaves abnormally?
options: investigate according to the vehicle instructions before continuing if a fault is indicated
cover the warning lamp
disconnect the ABS sensor
questions.explanation: Warning indicators should not be ignored; braking faults require assessment.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you notice an incorrect tachograph entry?
options: make the required correction or annotation with an auditable record
delete all records
ignore it because the vehicle unit stores data
questions.explanation: Records must accurately reflect activities; corrections should be traceable.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are driving down a hill in a low gear?
options: use the gear to help control speed and avoid continuous heavy service braking
select neutral to save fuel
switch off the engine
questions.explanation: A suitable gear helps control speed and reduces brake overheating.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you encounter standing water?
options: slow down and avoid sudden steering or braking
accelerate through it
brake sharply while in the water
questions.explanation: Standing water can cause loss of grip and aquaplaning.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a package label is missing or unreadable?
options: have the issue corrected before transport
guess the hazard class
copy a label from another package
questions.explanation: Packages must bear required hazard labels and marks.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are approaching a sharp bend with standing passengers?
options: reduce speed smoothly and avoid harsh manoeuvres
brake sharply at the bend
accelerate to shorten the turn
questions.explanation: Smooth driving helps protect standing passengers from falls.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle's load changes its height?
options: reassess the actual loaded height before route selection
use the empty vehicle height
assume load height is irrelevant
questions.explanation: Actual loaded dimensions determine clearance.

questions.question: What is the safest response when smoke enters the cab?
options: stop safely, evacuate if necessary and investigate only from a safe position
continue with windows open
ignore it if the engine still runs
questions.explanation: Smoke may indicate fire or a serious fault.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A lane control signal shows a red X above your lane?
options: continue if your vehicle fits
stop underneath the signal
leave the lane when safe and do not continue in it
questions.explanation: A red X means the lane is closed to traffic.

questions.question: What is the safest response when passing a cyclist?
options: pass closely to avoid crossing the centre line
sound the horn continuously
leave ample clearance and wait if the road is too narrow
questions.explanation: Give cyclists generous clearance; wait if a safe pass is not possible.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a daily walk-around inspection is due?
options: assume the previous driver's check covers every defect
check only the fuel level
complete the required checks before the vehicle is used
questions.explanation: A pre-use check helps identify defects before they cause harm.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load can move sideways on a flat platform?
options: secure only the front edge
rely on the side mirrors
fit suitable lateral restraints or blocking
questions.explanation: Restraints must prevent movement in all relevant directions.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a trailer begins to snake?
options: accelerate sharply
make sudden steering corrections
ease off the accelerator smoothly and avoid harsh steering or braking
questions.explanation: Smooth actions and reduced speed help control trailer oscillation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you perform other work while not driving?
options: record it as a break
leave the tachograph on driving
record it using the appropriate activity mode
questions.explanation: Other work is not a break and must be recorded correctly.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle's brakes pull to one side?
options: compensate by steering harder
continue at reduced speed indefinitely
stop safely and have the braking fault checked
questions.explanation: Uneven braking can cause loss of control and requires investigation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are planning a long professional journey?
options: rely on arriving before feeling tired
schedule no allowance for traffic
plan breaks, rest, route and contingencies before departure
questions.explanation: Planning reduces fatigue pressure and unsafe time decisions.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are transporting a gas cylinder?
options: leave it loose so it can be removed quickly
place it where it can roll
secure it against movement and protect valves as required
questions.explanation: Cylinders need suitable restraint and protection against damage.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger has mobility difficulties?
options: rush them to maintain schedule
move before they are seated or secure
allow adequate boarding time and use assistance equipment correctly
questions.explanation: Allowing safe boarding and using equipment correctly protects passengers.

questions.question: What is the safest response when an axle is overloaded although total gross weight is below the limit?
options: continue because gross weight is legal
inflate the overloaded axle's tyre
redistribute the load to meet axle limits
questions.explanation: Axle limits apply independently of the gross vehicle limit.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle is stranded in a live lane?
options: stand in front to direct traffic
push it alone without assessing risk
activate appropriate warnings and seek assistance while prioritising personal safety
questions.explanation: A stationary vehicle in a live lane is a serious hazard; protect people first.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A speed limit sign is displayed?
options: exceed it when carrying a light load
do not exceed the posted limit and drive to conditions
treat the limit as a target speed
questions.explanation: The posted limit is a maximum, not a target or guarantee of safety.

questions.question: What is the safest response when approaching a school entrance at busy times?
options: overtake stopped vehicles without checking
expect children and reduce speed
assume children will always use the crossing
questions.explanation: Children can move unpredictably; anticipate hazards around schools.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a defect develops during a journey?
options: continue regardless of severity
stop when safe, assess it and report it under company procedure
hide it until the end of the week
questions.explanation: Defects must be reported and unsafe vehicles taken out of service.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load is being unloaded on a slope?
options: allow the load to roll free
secure the vehicle and assess stability before unloading
release restraints while standing downhill
questions.explanation: Unloading can change stability and create serious crush hazards.

questions.question: What is the safest response when turning with a long articulated vehicle?
options: assume rear wheels follow front wheels
allow for off-tracking and check the space around the trailer
cut the corner tightly without checking
questions.explanation: Trailer wheels track inside the path of the tractor unit.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are waiting while available for work and the duration is known in advance?
options: record it as driving
record availability where that is the correct activity
record it as rest automatically
questions.explanation: Availability is distinct from rest and other work.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you approach a sharp bend in a loaded vehicle?
options: accelerate through the bend
reduce speed before entering the bend
brake hard while turning
questions.explanation: Braking before the bend reduces instability and rollover risk.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle's blind spot may contain a cyclist?
options: signal and move without checking
check mirrors and blind spots before turning or changing lanes
assume the cyclist will stop
questions.explanation: Signals do not replace observation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a fire occurs involving dangerous goods?
options: open packages to identify contents
raise the alarm, keep people away and follow emergency instructions
use any extinguisher without checking the hazard
questions.explanation: The correct response depends on the substance; protect people and follow instructions.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are about to reverse a bus in a depot?
options: assume pedestrians will hear the bus
check the area and use a trained guide where required
reverse quickly relying only on mirrors
questions.explanation: Large blind spots make reversing a serious risk.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are approaching a road with a width restriction?
options: fold mirrors while moving through traffic
check the full vehicle width including load and mirrors as relevant
assume the restriction applies only to cars
questions.explanation: Restrictions must be checked against the vehicle's actual dimensions.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you must use a warning triangle?
options: place it immediately behind a blind bend
place it only where lawful and safe, following the road and vehicle guidance
walk into fast traffic to position it
questions.explanation: Warning devices must never put the person placing them in danger.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A sign warns of a low bridge?
options: check the vehicle's actual height against the restriction
follow the vehicle ahead regardless
assume the sign applies only to buses
questions.explanation: Height restrictions must be checked against the actual loaded vehicle height.

questions.question: What is the safest response when using a mobile phone while driving?
options: do not hold or use a handheld phone while driving
read messages at red lights in traffic
hold it below the steering wheel
questions.explanation: Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited and distracting.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the brake pedal feels soft or travels unusually far?
options: stop safely and have the braking system checked
pump it at every junction and carry on
use the parking brake as the only brake
questions.explanation: Abnormal brake pedal behaviour may signal brake failure.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the centre of gravity is high and the route has bends?
options: reduce speed and negotiate bends smoothly
brake sharply while turning
take bends at the same speed as a car
questions.explanation: High loads increase rollover risk, especially during abrupt manoeuvres.

questions.question: What is the safest response when reversing to a loading bay with a trailer?
options: use a guide where possible and stop if the guide is lost from view
reverse quickly using mirrors only
keep moving if uncertain
questions.explanation: A guide and clear communication reduce reversing risk.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you drive under a valid exemption from EU drivers' hours rules?
options: check the exact exemption and any applicable national rules
assume all commercial driving is exempt
ignore road safety obligations
questions.explanation: Exemptions are specific; do not assume they apply to a journey.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the vehicle is carrying a liquid load that can surge?
options: anticipate movement and brake and steer smoothly
make abrupt changes to test the load
leave extra space unused
questions.explanation: Liquid surge can affect stability and vehicle control.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you encounter an aggressive driver?
options: remain calm, avoid confrontation and create space
respond with gestures and acceleration
block the vehicle deliberately
questions.explanation: Avoid escalating conflict and prioritise safety.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are asked to carry dangerous goods without the required documents?
options: do not depart until documentation requirements are met
rely on a text message
write a description from memory
questions.explanation: Required transport documents must accompany the load.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a passenger's belongings obstruct the aisle?
options: ask for them to be safely stowed
leave them as long as passengers can step over
place them in front of an exit
questions.explanation: Aisles and exits must remain clear for safe movement and evacuation.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you plan to use a residential shortcut?
options: consider road width, turning space, restrictions and vulnerable road users
assume a shorter route is always safer
follow a car regardless of access
questions.explanation: Heavy-vehicle route choice must consider access and safety.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a dangerous-goods incident occurs?
options: follow the written emergency instructions and keep people away
touch or smell the substance
wash the spill into a drain
questions.explanation: Dangerous goods incidents require substance-specific emergency action.

questions.question: What is the safest response when A sign indicates a mandatory direction?
options: choose another direction if convenient
ignore it when turning a large vehicle
follow the direction shown
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs prescribe the movement or route drivers must follow.

questions.question: What is the safest response when driving at night on an unlit road?
options: use full beam when following closely
drive using sidelights only
use appropriate headlights and dip them to avoid dazzling others
questions.explanation: Use headlights appropriate to visibility and dip to avoid dazzling.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a vehicle is heavily iced and windows are obscured?
options: clear only a small viewing hole
use wipers to remove thick ice while driving
clear all necessary windows, mirrors, lights and roof areas before moving
questions.explanation: The driver must have adequate visibility and prevent ice or snow becoming a hazard.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load covers the driver's view through mirrors or windows?
options: use a passenger to watch constantly
drive with the cab window open
rearrange it so required visibility is maintained
questions.explanation: The driver must maintain adequate observation and visibility.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the trailer is loaded close to its maximum?
options: check only tractor unit gross weight
assume trailer plate is optional
check axle loads, coupling limits and gross combination limits
questions.explanation: All relevant plated and statutory weight limits must be observed.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a driver is approaching a daily driving limit?
options: continue if the delivery is urgent
switch driver cards
plan a safe stop before the limit is reached
questions.explanation: Plan work to comply with driving limits and rest requirements.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are following another heavy vehicle?
options: drive close to reduce wind resistance
use the other vehicle's brake lights as your only warning
leave enough distance to see ahead and stop safely
questions.explanation: A safe following gap provides time and distance to react.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you drive a high-sided vehicle in exposed conditions?
options: ignore wind because the vehicle is heavy
drive close to another vehicle for shelter
check wind warnings and consider whether conditions are safe for the vehicle
questions.explanation: Crosswinds can destabilise high-sided vehicles, especially when empty.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you are unsure which fire extinguisher is suitable?
options: use water on every type of fire
approach the fire to inspect the label
follow the emergency instructions and use only if trained and safe
questions.explanation: Some substances react dangerously with unsuitable extinguishing agents.

questions.question: What is the safest response when the bus is approaching a stop on a slippery surface?
options: brake sharply at the last moment
turn sharply to reach the kerb
brake progressively and position the bus carefully
questions.explanation: Smooth control reduces skidding and passenger falls.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a load is close to the maximum permitted height?
options: estimate from the driver's seat
rely on a warning device alone
measure it accurately and plan a route with adequate clearance
questions.explanation: Accurate measurement and route planning prevent bridge strikes.

questions.question: What is the safest response when you experience a sudden steering failure?
options: accelerate to restore steering
turn sharply onto the verge
ease off, avoid abrupt manoeuvres and bring the vehicle to a controlled stop
questions.explanation: Controlled deceleration and avoiding abrupt inputs reduce loss-of-control risk.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if A triangular warning sign is approaching?
options: reduce speed and prepare for the hazard
ignore it unless traffic is present
accelerate to pass it quickly
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if approaching a zebra crossing with pedestrians waiting?
options: slow down and be prepared to stop
sound the horn to make them hurry
overtake a vehicle that has stopped
questions.explanation: Drivers must approach crossings carefully and give way as required.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a tyre has a deep cut or exposed cords?
options: do not use the vehicle until the defect is rectified
inflate it and continue
cover the damage with tape
questions.explanation: Tyre structural damage can cause sudden failure.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a load could slide forward during emergency braking?
options: use suitable restraints against forward movement
rely on friction alone in every case
place loose material on top
questions.explanation: Loads must be restrained against forces in normal driving and emergency manoeuvres.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if coupling a trailer to a tractor unit?
options: check compatibility, engagement and locking indicators
assume it has coupled because the trailer is raised
pull away without checking
questions.explanation: A visual and physical coupling check helps prevent trailer separation.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you reach 4 hours 30 minutes of cumulative driving?
options: take a 45-minute break unless a valid split-break arrangement applies
take a 15-minute break only
continue until 5 hours
questions.explanation: The standard EU break is 45 minutes after 4.5 hours driving.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if the vehicle's speed is doubled?
options: recognise that braking distance can increase by roughly four times under otherwise similar conditions
expect braking distance to double exactly
expect no change
questions.explanation: Braking distance rises approximately with the square of speed in idealised conditions.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?
options: stop at a safe place and take appropriate rest
open a window and continue indefinitely
turn up the radio
questions.explanation: Fatigue impairs attention and reaction; do not drive when unfit.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a package may contain dangerous goods but its contents are unknown?
options: do not accept or handle it until correctly identified
open it to smell the contents
assume it is ordinary freight
questions.explanation: Dangerous goods must be identified before applying handling and transport rules.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if passengers are still boarding?
options: remain stopped until boarding is complete and it is safe to move
move slowly while doors are open
sound the horn to hurry passengers
questions.explanation: The bus should move only when boarding is complete and doors are closed.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if your loaded vehicle is taller than a bridge's signed clearance?
options: do not proceed; choose a suitable alternative route
drive slowly under the bridge
follow a lower vehicle through
questions.explanation: A vehicle must not exceed a height restriction.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if your vehicle breaks down on a high-speed road?
options: protect yourself and others and get to a safe place if possible
attempt repairs in a live lane
stand behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes first; follow the road's breakdown procedure.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if A red-bordered circular sign is displayed?
options: treat it as an information sign
ignore it if the road is clear
obey the restriction shown by its symbol
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circular signs generally indicate prohibitions or restrictions.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if turning left across a cycle lane?
options: turn without checking because you signal
accelerate across the lane
check mirrors and blind spots and give way to cyclists
questions.explanation: Cyclists may be alongside; check carefully before turning.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a brake warning lamp remains illuminated?
options: ignore it if the parking brake is released
disconnect the warning buzzer
investigate and resolve the fault before driving
questions.explanation: A brake warning may indicate a serious safety defect.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a load is much heavier on one side?
options: leave it if gross weight is below the limit
inflate tyres on the heavier side
redistribute it to avoid uneven axle loading and instability
questions.explanation: Uneven loading can overload an axle and affect handling.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if the fifth-wheel jaws may not be locked?
options: test it at road speed
rely on the air lines to hold it
do not move until the coupling is correctly engaged and locked
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel must securely lock around the kingpin.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you split the standard 45-minute driving break?
options: take 30 minutes followed by 15 minutes
take three 15-minute periods
take at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes
questions.explanation: The permitted split is at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a heavy vehicle is fully laden?
options: assume load has no effect
follow closer because the vehicle is heavier
allow for the vehicle's mass and condition when judging stopping distance
questions.explanation: Vehicle mass and braking performance affect stopping behaviour.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you approach a blind bend?
options: overtake if the road seems quiet
sound the horn and use the centre line
reduce speed and keep well within your lane
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop within the road you can see to be clear.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if dangerous goods are offered for carriage?
options: rely only on the sender's verbal assurance
remove labels to avoid alarm
check classification, packaging, marking and documentation requirements
questions.explanation: ADR controls include classification, packaging, marks, labels and documents.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a passenger using a wheelchair boards?
options: leave the wheelchair unsecured
place luggage in the wheelchair space
use the designated space and approved restraint system as instructed
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle's accessibility equipment and securement procedure.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a route has a weight-restricted bridge?
options: cross if the bridge looks strong
drive over the centre line
check the vehicle's relevant weight against the restriction and use another route if necessary
questions.explanation: Weight restrictions must be obeyed.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you are involved in a collision?
options: leave without checking for injuries
move injured people unnecessarily
stop, make the scene safe where possible and provide required details and assistance
questions.explanation: Drivers involved in collisions have duties to stop and provide assistance and details.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if A Garda is directing traffic against a traffic signal?
options: copy the vehicle ahead
follow the Garda's direction when safe
obey the signal regardless
questions.explanation: A Garda's direction takes precedence over traffic signals.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if approaching a roundabout?
options: change lanes abruptly on the roundabout
choose the correct lane and follow signs and road markings
always use the left lane for every exit
questions.explanation: Lane choice and signals depend on the exit and road markings.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a headlamp is not working before a night journey?
options: drive faster to reduce exposure
have it repaired before setting out
use hazard lights instead
questions.explanation: Required lighting must be in working order.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if the vehicle's gross weight would exceed its plated limit?
options: inflate tyres to increase capacity
remove or redistribute load until within permitted limits
drive only on quiet roads
questions.explanation: The plated maximum weight must not be exceeded.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if connecting trailer air lines?
options: leave a line disconnected for short trips
connect the correct lines securely and check for leaks
swap line colours if they fit
questions.explanation: Correct air connections are essential for trailer braking.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if planning daily driving under the standard EU rule?
options: drive 12 hours if the vehicle is a bus
normally keep driving to 9 hours, with 10 hours allowed twice weekly
drive 10 hours every day
questions.explanation: The normal daily driving limit is 9 hours, extendable to 10 hours twice a week.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if the road surface is wet?
options: brake later to keep traffic flowing
increase following distance and reduce speed
use the same gap as on dry roads
questions.explanation: Wet surfaces reduce grip and can increase stopping distances.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you see children near the roadside?
options: maintain speed to avoid confusing them
anticipate sudden movement and reduce speed
assume they will remain on the footpath
questions.explanation: Children may move unpredictably; prepare to stop.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a driver is assigned an ADR-regulated load?
options: borrow another driver's certificate
ensure required training and certificate are valid for the task
assume an ordinary driving licence is sufficient
questions.explanation: Some dangerous-goods carriage requires specialised driver training and certification.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a passenger is standing near the doors?
options: close the doors against them
ensure passengers are safely accommodated before moving
accelerate gently to help them balance
questions.explanation: Passengers must be safely positioned before the bus moves.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you are planning a route for an articulated vehicle?
options: assume every road accommodates heavy vehicles
check restrictions for height, width, length and weight
use a car navigation route without checking
questions.explanation: Route planning must account for the vehicle's actual dimensions and mass.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if someone is seriously injured?
options: give food or drink
call 112 or 999 and follow the operator's instructions
move them immediately in every case
questions.explanation: Emergency services can provide guidance; avoid unnecessary movement of injured people.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if An amber traffic light appears as you approach?
options: stop if you can do so safely
accelerate in every situation
reverse immediately
questions.explanation: Amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping could cause an accident.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if reversing a large vehicle?
options: avoid reversing where possible and use a competent guide if needed
rely only on mirrors
reverse quickly to minimise delay
questions.explanation: Large vehicle blind spots make reversing especially hazardous.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a mirror is loose and cannot hold its position?
options: repair it before driving
adjust it once and ignore movement
drive using only the interior mirror
questions.explanation: Drivers need secure, correctly adjusted mirrors for observation.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a load projects beyond the vehicle?
options: ensure it is within legal requirements and properly marked where required
assume any projection is allowed at night
leave it unmarked if the journey is short
questions.explanation: Projections must comply with dimensional and marking rules.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a trailer breakaway device is fitted?
options: connect and route it as specified by the manufacturer
tie it to a movable part of the coupling
leave it disconnected
questions.explanation: A breakaway device is intended to activate braking if separation occurs.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if planning a driver's weekly driving?
options: do not exceed 56 hours in a week
do not exceed 60 hours in a week
use 56 hours as a daily limit
questions.explanation: The standard weekly driving limit is 56 hours.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you descend a long steep gradient?
options: select a suitable low gear before the descent and use appropriate auxiliary braking
coast in neutral
keep the clutch depressed
questions.explanation: Engine braking and appropriate gear selection help prevent brake overheating.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you are driving in strong crosswinds?
options: reduce speed and be alert to exposed sections and high-sided vehicle movement
increase speed to stabilise the vehicle
steer abruptly against every gust
questions.explanation: High-sided vehicles are vulnerable to crosswinds.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a dangerous-goods package is damaged and leaking?
options: keep clear, avoid contact and follow emergency instructions
handle it with bare hands
wash it into a drain
questions.explanation: A leak may expose people and the environment; follow emergency procedures.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a passenger asks to alight between designated stops?
options: stop only where permitted and safe under the service rules
stop immediately in a live lane
open the doors while moving
questions.explanation: Passenger safety and stopping restrictions must be observed.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a load makes the vehicle wider than usual?
options: ensure the movement complies with legal limits and any required permissions
drive close to the kerb
assume warning lights make any width lawful
questions.explanation: Abnormal dimensions may require special conditions or authorisation.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a vehicle fire starts?
options: stop safely, evacuate people and call emergency services
open the engine compartment fully immediately
continue to the next exit
questions.explanation: Evacuate and raise the alarm; do not put yourself at risk.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if A green traffic light is showing but the junction is blocked?
options: enter and block the junction
sound the horn until traffic moves
wait until your exit is clear
questions.explanation: A green signal does not permit you to obstruct a junction.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if driving on a narrow rural road?
options: assume oncoming traffic will reverse
drive partly on the footpath
reduce speed and be prepared to stop at a safe passing place
questions.explanation: Narrow roads require speed adjustment and consideration for other users.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if the steering feels unusually loose?
options: continue if the road is straight
increase speed to test it
stop safely and arrange inspection
questions.explanation: Steering defects can cause loss of control.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a curtain-sided trailer carries a dense load?
options: assume the curtain alone secures all cargo
place all weight against the rear doors
use suitable load restraint; curtains are not automatically load restraints
questions.explanation: Curtains may not be designed to restrain a load unless specifically rated.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a trailer's electrical plug is connected?
options: assume the plug guarantees all lamps work
check only the brake lights
check trailer lights and indicators operate correctly
questions.explanation: A walk-around check should confirm all required trailer lights operate.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if checking driving over two consecutive weeks?
options: keep total driving within 112 hours
count only the first week
keep total driving within 90 hours
questions.explanation: The two-week cumulative driving limit is 90 hours.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if brakes smell hot after a long descent?

questions.explanation: Smooth control reduces skidding and passenger falls.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if a load is close to the maximum permitted height?
options: estimate from the driver's seat
rely on a warning device alone
measure it accurately and plan a route with adequate clearance
questions.explanation: Accurate measurement and route planning prevent bridge strikes.

questions.question: As a professional driver, what should you do if you experience a sudden steering failure?
options: accelerate to restore steering
turn sharply onto the verge
ease off, avoid abrupt manoeuvres and bring the vehicle to a controlled stop
questions.explanation: Controlled deceleration and avoiding abrupt inputs reduce loss-of-control risk.

questions.question: Which action is correct when A triangular warning sign is approaching?
options: reduce speed and prepare for the hazard
ignore it unless traffic is present
accelerate to pass it quickly
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead.

questions.question: Which action is correct when approaching a zebra crossing with pedestrians waiting?
options: slow down and be prepared to stop
sound the horn to make them hurry
overtake a vehicle that has stopped
questions.explanation: Drivers must approach crossings carefully and give way as required.

questions.question: Which action is correct when a tyre has a deep cut or exposed cords?
options: do not use the vehicle until the defect is rectified
inflate it and continue
cover the damage with tape
questions.explanation: Tyre structural damage can cause sudden failure.

questions.question: Which action is correct when a load could slide forward during emergency braking?
options: use suitable restraints against forward movement
rely on friction alone in every case
place loose material on top
questions.explanation: Loads must be restrained against forces in normal driving and emergency manoeuvres.

questions.question: Which action is correct when coupling a trailer to a tractor unit?
options: check compatibility, engagement and locking indicators
assume it has coupled because the trailer is raised
pull away without checking
questions.explanation: A visual and physical coupling check helps prevent trailer separation.

questions.question: Which action is correct when you reach 4 hours 30 minutes of cumulative driving?
options: take a 45-minute break unless a valid split-break arrangement applies
take a 15-minute break only
continue until 5 hours
questions.explanation: The standard EU break is 45 minutes after 4.5 hours driving.

questions.question: Which action is correct when the vehicle's speed is doubled?
options: recognise that braking distance can increase by roughly four times under otherwise similar conditions
expect braking distance to double exactly
expect no change
questions.explanation: Braking distance rises approximately with the square of speed in idealised conditions.

questions.question: Which action is correct when you feel sleepy while driving?
options: stop at a safe place and take appropriate rest
open a window and continue indefinitely
turn up the radio
questions.explanation: Fatigue impairs attention and reaction; do not drive when unfit.

questions.question: Which action is correct when a package may contain dangerous goods but its contents are unknown?
options: do not accept or handle it until correctly identified
open it to smell the contents
assume it is ordinary freight
questions.explanation: Dangerous goods must be identified before applying handling and transport rules.

questions.question: Which action is correct when passengers are still boarding?
options: remain stopped until boarding is complete and it is safe to move
move slowly while doors are open
sound the horn to hurry passengers
questions.explanation: The bus should move only when boarding is complete and doors are closed.

questions.question: Which action is correct when your loaded vehicle is taller than a bridge's signed clearance?
options: do not proceed; choose a suitable alternative route
drive slowly under the bridge
follow a lower vehicle through
questions.explanation: A vehicle must not exceed a height restriction.

questions.question: Which action is correct when your vehicle breaks down on a high-speed road?
options: protect yourself and others and get to a safe place if possible
attempt repairs in a live lane
stand behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes first; follow the road's breakdown procedure.

questions.question: Which action is correct when A red-bordered circular sign is displayed?
options: treat it as an information sign
ignore it if the road is clear
obey the restriction shown by its symbol
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circular signs generally indicate prohibitions or restrictions.

questions.question: Which action is correct when turning left across a cycle lane?
options: turn without checking because you signal
accelerate across the lane
check mirrors and blind spots and give way to cyclists
questions.explanation: Cyclists may be alongside; check carefully before turning.

questions.question: Which action is correct when a brake warning lamp remains illuminated?
options: ignore it if the parking brake is released
disconnect the warning buzzer
investigate and resolve the fault before driving
questions.explanation: A brake warning may indicate a serious safety defect.

questions.question: Which action is correct when a load is much heavier on one side?
options: leave it if gross weight is below the limit
inflate tyres on the heavier side
redistribute it to avoid uneven axle loading and instability
questions.explanation: Uneven loading can overload an axle and affect handling.

questions.question: Which action is correct when the fifth-wheel jaws may not be locked?
options: test it at road speed
rely on the air lines to hold it
do not move until the coupling is correctly engaged and locked
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel must securely lock around the kingpin.

questions.question: Which action is correct when you split the standard 45-minute driving break?
options: take 30 minutes followed by 15 minutes
take three 15-minute periods
take at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes
